caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Nuro, Inc.
claims: PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) (prospective — use of registry info in hiring); ICRAA §§1786.16, 1786.40 (prospective); FCRA §§1681b(b)(2)(A), 1681b(b)(3), 1681e(b), 1681i (prospective); CA Fair Chance Act, Gov. Code §12952 (prospective); UCL §17200 (prospective)
defendants: Nuro, Inc. (prospective). Checkr (prospective vendor defendant, user-stated — not confirmed in any document yet).
key_facts: On Sep. 9, 2026, Brendan Ngwa Nforbi applied via Indeed to Nuro, Inc. for Autonomous Vehicle Operator, San Francisco (overnight shift, 12-month duration); Greenhouse auto-replied the same evening. On Sep. 10, Elizabeth Gonzalez (Recruiter, Operations, eligonzalez@nuro.ai) via GoodTime.io invited him to submit availability for a 45-minute Google Meet interview (Nuro values + technical/troubleshooting). On Sep. 15, Crystal Garcia (Recruiting Coordinator, crgarcia@nuro.ai) sent the calendar invite: Google Meet Wed Sep. 16, 4:30–5:15 p.m. PDT with James Craig (Nuro Values & Problem Solving) plus CodePair technical instructions; Elizabeth Gonzalez confirmed the same day (reply to confirm; no LLM/AI notetakers). The interview took place Sep. 16. On Sep. 17, Nuro advanced him to an onsite 45-minute Driving Evaluation and Crystal Garcia sent the license-requirements email: valid driver's license, 3 consecutive years of licensure with no gaps, California license in California — and an official DMV driving record / Motor Vehicle Report (MVR) is named as acceptable documentation. The onsite invite set Fri Sep. 18, 12:00–12:45 p.m. PDT, rear of the Safeway parking lot, 4950 Mission St, San Francisco (white Prius; Nuro safety vest; instructor (650) 933-2394). The driving evaluation took place Sep. 18. He signed Nuro's DocuSign NDA + Exhibit A site-visit liability waiver (Envelope ID B1019EC0-467E-8D8F-8389-021C270CBC16, countersigned by Michelle Nguyen, HR Program Manager): one-way NDA, interviewing-only permitted use, 3-year survival; waiver assumes site-visit risk, holds Nuro harmless for site participation, and includes a CC §1542 waiver and likeness consent. As of Sep. 18: no background-check authorization or disclosure signed, no Checkr report, no adverse action. Checkr as vendor is user-stated, not yet documented.
